Security.label: Operational Friction
Security.why: Zero Trust mandates continuous identity and device re-verification, causing delays during incident response and system recovery; this friction can impede reliability, as responders must complete additional verification steps even during emergencies.

Cost.label: Increased Cost
Cost.why: Ensuring reliable systems under Zero Trust incurs extra costs—redundancy, failover, advanced identity providers, network segmentation, and audit systems all add significant expense beyond traditional reliability spend.

Operational.label: Increased Complexity
Operational.why: Implementing resilient systems with Zero Trust creates complex operational workflows including continual trust verification post-recovery, elaborate runbooks, and incident diagnosis that is masked by security logging.

Performance.label: Increased Latency
Performance.why: Zero Trust’s added health checks, authentication, and segmentation increase network and compute overhead, introducing latency during failover events, API calls, and segmented traffic inspection.

Reliability.label: Operational Friction
Reliability.why: Security controls slow rapid remediation since every system action must comply with authentication and authorization; swift restoration of reliability faces delays due to ongoing access policies.

Cost.label: Increased Cost
Cost.why: Zero Trust demands investment in multifactor authentication, device monitoring, policy-driven access controls, raising operational costs for secure cloud environments and expanding licensing and support requirements.

Operational.label: Reduced Velocity
Operational.why: Continuous verification required by Zero Trust slows down deployment and automation pipelines; every resource, workload, and user needs registration and compliance checks, hindering rapid operational changes and releases.

Performance.label: Performance Overhead
Performance.why: Frequent security checks and segmentation require additional CPU, memory, and network resources, detracting from workload performance and increasing latency and throughput losses.

Reliability.label: Reduced Resiliency
Reliability.why: Reducing spend typically cuts redundancy and monitoring, undermining resilience and increasing risk of extended outages or catastrophic failure.

Security.label: Reduced Controls
Security.why: Limiting budget for security leads to fewer technical safeguards—less thorough device management, weaker identity verification, and shorter audit logs, raising risk exposure.

Operational.label: Reduced Observability
Operational.why: Cutting cost on operational tooling results in diminished diagnostics, observability, and automation, leaving teams with reduced insight into system health for troubleshooting and compliance.

Performance.label: Underprovisioning
Performance.why: Efforts to minimize cost lead to under-provisioned resources, causing slow response times and higher latency during high traffic or computational spikes.

Reliability.label: Destabilization Risk
Reliability.why: Rapid operational changes such as deployments and reconfigurations can destabilize resilient architectures without proper failover and backup alignment.

Security.label: Increased Surface Area
Security.why: Operational expansions, automated resource vending, and opening new environments increase network and workload attack surface unless tightly governed, leading to new security gaps.

Cost.label: Increased Tooling Spend
Cost.why: Enhancing operational excellence requires costly investments in automation platforms, observability tools, and orchestration solutions, driving up cloud tooling budgets.

Performance.label: Resource Utilization
Performance.why: Operational efficiency may maximize resource utilization for savings, occasionally throttling peak performance as resources are pooled and decommissioned.

Reliability.label: Increased Density Risk
Reliability.why: Maximizing resource density for peak performance raises the risk that a single hardware failure will cascade across tightly packed critical workloads.

Security.label: Reduced Segmentation
Security.why: Eliminating network segmentation to optimize speed makes lateral threat movement possible, exposing workloads to increased risk in exchange for performance gains.

Cost.label: Overprovisioning Cost
Cost.why: Maintaining surplus compute, memory, or bandwidth to guarantee low latency demands excess spend, with costs rising as capacity is reserved for rare peaks.

Operational.label: Increased Complexity
Operational.why: Performance optimization involves specialized operational tuning, frequent adjustments, and custom scaling rules, demanding additional expertise and time from operations teams.
